issue.title: Spotify episodes become first-class podcast references
issue.description: Every Spotify episode link given to `bob ref create`, capture, or Keep becomes one deduplicated `podcasts` reference. Its PDF is an episode dossier: cover, show, date, duration, clickable chapters, full show notes, and a highlightable transcript when the publisher's own feed proves the match. Every other Spotify link is refused, or is kept as an ordinary item, with a hint that says what to do instead. No Spotify link reaches the article engine again.

payload.entry: API for transcript_dossier (os.9): podcast/feed.rs find_feed_item(&EpisodeMetadata, PodcastEnrich, scratch, deadline: Instant, progress) -> FeedOutcome {Matched(FeedItem), NoFeed(reason), NoMatch(reason; ties start "ambiguous:"), DeadlineExceeded, Off}. Off makes no request; DeadlineExceeded maps to "feed lookup stopped after 45 s". FeedItem: feed_url/feed_host (post-redirect), guid, title, pub_date, duration_secs (drift guard), notes_html (content:encoded else description, invisibles stripped), transcripts [{url,mime,language,rel}], chapters Option<FeedChaptersLink{url,mime}>, matched_on + matched_on_label() ("title, date" for the dry-run line). fetch_feed_chapters(&link, scratch, deadline, progress) -> ChaptersOutcome {Chapters(Vec<notes::Chapter>), Ignored(reason), DeadlineExceeded}; parse_chapters_json is pure. fetch.rs gained fetch_url_before(url, dest, max_time, max_bytes, deadline, progress) + deadline_spent(deadline) — use them for the 10 MiB transcript download so one 45 s budget covers feed + transcript. Config: HighlightsConfig::podcast_enrich() parses highlights.podcasts.enrich auto|off (default auto); its docs (configuration.md + highlights-create.md) are still owed by transcript_dossier per the plan. Test seam: podcast::test_support::FakeSpotify now has serve_url(exact URL) and an itunes surface.

API for transcript_dossier (bob-cli-os.9): podcast::transcript::preferred_offer(&item.transcripts, |t| (t.mime.as_str(), t.url.as_str())) -> Option<(&FeedTranscript, TranscriptFormat)> picks JSON > VTT > SRT > HTML > text (specific MIME wins; text/plain, octet-stream, or empty defer to the URL extension). parse_transcript(bytes, mime, url, duration_ms: Option<u64>) -> Result<Transcript, TranscriptDrop>. Transcript { format, paragraphs: Vec<Paragraph { start_secs: Option<u32>, speaker: Option<String>, text }> (Serialize), words, roles_inferred, names_from_file }. TranscriptDrop Display is the text after "transcript dropped: ". TranscriptFormat::as_str() = json/vtt/srt/html/text (payload), label() = JSON/VTT/SRT/HTML/text (provenance line). format_clock(secs) = m:ss / h:mm:ss. start_secs is None for text transcripts and for a paragraph that opens inside the cue that opened the previous paragraph (one long cue never stamps two paragraphs), so the renderer and chapter_marks must skip None starts.

Added src/native/highlights_ref/podcast/transcript.rs: pure parse_transcript for Podcasting 2.0 JSON, WebVTT (header, cue ids, settings, NOTE/STYLE/REGION, voices incl. several per cue, inline tags, ruby text, entities), SRT (CRLF, tags, {\\an8}), HTML (//

), and text; preferred_offer with JSON > VTT > SRT > HTML > text; drops with reasons (not text, unsupported, malformed, empty, <200 words, >120,000 words, last cue outside 50-110% of a known duration); diarization tokens -> Speaker N in first-appearance order, Host/Guest only for exactly two diarized speakers with >=10 questions and >=3x question rate, names never guessed; paragraphs merge same-speaker cues, close at the first sentence end after 95 words, force at 160, break on speaker change and text blank lines. Fixtures: trimmed real Pragmatic Engineer VTT (first 3 min, byte-for-byte) plus SRT/JSON/HTML/text re-encodings. 32 unit tests cover every format, garbage drops, diarized and voice-tagged files, paragraph bounds, and the question-rate rule both ways. Verified: just check green (fmt, workspace clippy gate, full workspace tests) on the tree rebased onto origin/master 3ce97d73; no docs or CLI surface changed.
